title: The sell-ceiling config tests prove buildReconcileConfig reads MEV_SELL_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI when called with leg "sell", but no production strategy ever passes "sell", so the registered defect that private sells run with the buy ceiling passes them green

evidence.note: loadReconcileConfig calls buildReconcileConfig(process.env, SELL_GAS_LIMIT, 3, leg) directly
"the sell leg reads its OWN ceiling": asserted only on the direct call with leg "sell"
the ceiling is the sell value only when leg is "sell"
the strategy calls buildReconcileConfig with no leg (buy); passthrough.ts:83 and bloxroute.ts:104 the same

sibling_sites_checked: mevStrategies/gasMultiplier.test.ts and inclusionReconciliation.test.ts (CR-01 clamp cases) drive the strategies with the default buy leg; exitEngine tests mock escalatePrivateSell. No unit test drives a private sell through a strategy and inspects its fee ceiling.
severity_rationale: S3: the test is real for the function but its claim ("the sell leg uses the SELL ceiling") does not hold on any live path; the hidden registered defect AUD-TX-010 is S2.
recommendation: Phase 28: assert the ceiling a private sell actually submits with (escalatePrivateSell through a strategy), not the config helper alone.
affected_cases: Test 1 — sell leg uses the SELL ceiling (25 gwei) when MEV_SELL_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI=25
Test 5 — sell ceiling defaults to 25 gwei when MEV_SELL_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI is unset
respects an operator override of the sell ceiling (e.g. 40 gwei)
escaped_regression: Today's code already escapes (AUD-TX-010): every strategy calls buildReconcileConfig without a leg (flashbots.ts:182), so private sells use the buy ceiling while these cases stay green.
